tourist_visa.extension: USD 3 per day with a minimum of 15 days (i.e. USD 45 minimum), per the DoI fees table ('Extension $3/day (min. 15 days)').
tourist_visa.annual_maximum: Extension up to 150 days total per visa year (January–December).
tourist_visa.mission_visa_validity: A visa obtained from a Nepali diplomatic mission must be used to enter within six months of issue; stay counts from the entry date.
gratis: SAARC citizens (except Afghanistan) – up to 30 days on first visit in a visa year
Officials from China, Brazil, Russia and Thailand (reciprocal)
tourist_visa.process: Fill the Arrival Card and online tourist visa form (online before arrival or on TIA kiosks; receipt valid 15 days), pay at the bank counter, then go to the immigration desk. ETA/visa fee can also be paid online via mobile banking, ConnectIPS, eSewa, Khalti or debit/credit card.
tourist_visa.us_reciprocity: US citizens: 5-year tourist visa, 180 days stay per year, USD 160 (bank statement min. USD 10,000, health insurance, police report).

visa.work_rules_note: DoI: 'Only foreign nationals holding a Working Visa are allowed to accept employment and work in Nepal.' DoI pages do not address remote work for foreign employers.
visa.residential_visa_note: DoI lists a Residential visa for foreigners living in Nepal without business (income ≥ USD 20,000/yr, proof of age ≥ 60 or retirement, health certificate, etc.). Fee shown as USD 1,200/year on the fees table but 'New: USD 700/yr, Renewal: USD 1,200' on the Visa Information page — inconsistent on the official site. Not a nomad visa.

digital_nomad_visa.summary: Proposed in the Office of the Prime Minister's Economic Reform Implementing Work Plan 2025 (reported 28 May 2025): a one-time five-year multiple-entry digital nomad visa with income > USD 1,500/month or bank balance > USD 20,000, health insurance ≥ USD 100,000, 5% income tax after 186 days in a calendar year; 'expected to be implemented within a year'. As of 2026-09-26 the Department of Immigration's visa-fees and visa-information pages list no digital nomad category (only Diplomatic, Official, Tourist, Working, Press, Relation, Marriage, Study, Business, NRN, Residential, Transit and US-reciprocity visas). No enacted policy, gazette notice or application process was found.

proposed_terms.tax: 5% income tax if residing > 186 days in a calendar year
proposed_terms.other: residential approval ≥1 year at a time, bank accounts, vehicle registration, foreign licence accreditation

season.summary: Monsoon rains fall June–September; in the Kathmandu Valley and Pokhara they typically come as 'an hour or two of rain every two or three days'. Autumn (October–December) has little dust and is called the best season for the hills and mountains. Winter (January–March) nights in Kathmandu often drop to about freezing. April–June brings rhododendron blooms, with Kathmandu around 30 °C.

tips.tip: Scheduled load-shedding ended: NEA declared Nepal 'load-shedding free' from 14 May 2018 (domestic load-shedding had ended mid-April 2017). Unscheduled outages still happen — Nomads.com rates the power grid 'Bad' in both cities, a 2024 Pokhara guide says 'Pokhara does experience regular power outages' and advises asking hosts about backup, and a 2026 Kathmandu café guide says generator backup 'matters more than people expect'.

neighborhoods.name: Thamel
neighborhoods.description: Kathmandu's backpacker district: 'a maze of alleys crammed with handicraft shops, guest houses, and cafés' whose core is traffic-free (Wikivoyage). Wikivoyage notes virtually all tourist accommodation is in Thamel; Nomadista calls it loud and busy but central.

neighborhoods.name: Jhamsikhel / Sanepa (Lalitpur)
neighborhoods.description: A street in Jhamsikhel 'popular with expatriates and locals' is informally known as 'Jhamel' — 'much more chilled out' than Thamel (Wikivoyage Patan). Tiny Living calls Sanepa/Jhamsikhel/Pulchowk 'the single best remote-work cafe density in Kathmandu Valley'.

sources.name: Tiny Living – Best Cafes for Remote Work in Kathmandu (2026)

neighborhoods.name: Patan Durbar area (Lalitpur)
neighborhoods.description: Patan, about 4 km from Thamel, is 'fast becoming an area of preference for those in the know looking for more space and less chaos'; many expatriate communities live there because INGOs and some embassies are located in Patan (Wikivoyage). Patan Durbar Square is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

neighborhoods.name: Boudha (Boudhanath)
neighborhoods.description: East Kathmandu area around one of the largest Buddhist stupas in the world, surrounded by at least 29 Tibetan gompas; a UNESCO site since 1979 (Wikivoyage). Wikivoyage notes 'some good deals' on accommodation around Boudha; Nomadista describes a calm, international, spiritual vibe.

neighborhoods.name: Lazimpat
neighborhoods.description: Central Kathmandu's embassy and hotel strip: CIWEC travel clinic is 'Located centrally in Lazimpat, across from the British embassy' (Wikivoyage). Nabin Gaire recommends the Himalayan Java branch in Lazimpat's Bluebird Mall for focused work.

neighborhoods.name: Lakeside
neighborhoods.description: Where most visitors stay, along Phewa (Fewa) Lake; Wikivoyage says the lakeside strip 'now feels more like Khao San Road' and is the best place for live music. A Way Abroad (2024) suggests any place within a 20-minute walk of Phewa Lake is a good base.

sources.name: A Way Abroad – A Digital Nomad's Guide to Living in Pokhara, Nepal

neighborhoods.name: Damside
neighborhoods.description: Tourist area by Phewa Lake (Wikivoyage lists hotels and restaurants on Damside Marg/Damside Rd); Wikivoyage: 'Virtually all tourist accommodations are in Lakeside and Damside, near Phewa Lake.'

neighborhoods.name: Sarangkot
neighborhoods.description: Hill above the lake, known for sunrise views of the Annapurna range. Wikivoyage: around 12 guesthouses uphill 'offer better views and less air pollution, but are much more expensive'; they are a 20-minute walk uphill on gravel from the Sarangkot taxi stand.

season.summary: A Way Abroad: winter (Dec–Feb) gets cold; June–August is monsoon, with heavy rain, heat and humidity. Nomads.com monthly median rainfall: 261–444 mm/month May–Sep, under 45 mm Nov–Apr.

tips.tip: Scheduled load-shedding ended: NEA declared Nepal 'load-shedding free' from 14 May 2018 (domestic load-shedding had ended mid-April 2017). Unscheduled outages still happen — Nomads.com rates the power grid 'Bad' in both cities, a 2024 Pokhara guide says 'Pokhara does experience regular power outages' and advises asking hosts about backup, and a 2026 Kathmandu café guide says generator backup 'matters more than people expect'.

tips.tip: Nomads.com marks both cities 'No, cash only (esp. for foreigners)'. Wikivoyage: not all Thamel ATMs accept foreign cards and most that do charge Rs 650 per transaction; Standard Chartered and Nabil ATMs have the highest limit (Rs 35,000 per transaction).

Since 28 Aug 2025, visitors using Alipay+ wallets (Alipay, KakaoPay, GCash, Touch 'n Go, AlipayHK, TrueMoney, Tinaba; 11+ countries including China, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Germany and Italy) can scan and pay at eSewa Business / Fonepay QR merchants. Indian visitors can pay the same QR codes with UPI apps (PhonePe, BHIM, Google Pay). The sources do not say whether foreigners can open their own eSewa/Khalti wallets.
